questions.chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes “electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS)”?

options.label: A
options.text: A fundamental reaction where an electrophile replaces a hydrogen atom on an aromatic ring while maintaining the aromatic sextet.

options.label: B
options.text: An aromatic substituent that donates electron density through resonance or induction, directing incoming electrophiles predominantly to ortho and para positions.

options.label: C
options.text: A substituent that withdraws electron density from an aromatic ring, decreasing its reactivity toward electrophilic substitution.

options.label: D
options.text: The substitution of an alkyl group onto an aromatic ring using an alkyl halide and a Lewis acid catalyst such as AlCl3.

questions.correct_answer: A fundamental reaction where an electrophile replaces a hydrogen atom on an aromatic ring while maintaining the aromatic sextet.
questions.explanation: A accurate description of electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS) is: A fundamental reaction where an electrophile replaces a hydrogen atom on an aromatic ring while maintaining the aromatic sextet.
